question: How should typed extensions contribute and reconfigure schema and behavior without duplicate configuration authorities?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model, then widened it on 2026-10-04 to every existing ledger item. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was closed, with a latest stop verdict, at queue position 4 in the plite-core group. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: Schema, state fields, APIs and plugin configuration publish together or roll back together.
Replaceable ownership (a slot) differs from prerequisites (dependencies) and from conflicts.
Neutral ordered contributions serve raw transfer, DOM data-transfer and authored producers; Plate keeps product policy.
Plugins have no config channel. Immutable inputs stay in factory closures, and Plugin stays flat except on.* (docs/vision/plite.md).
Schema is the sole first-party AST-shape truth, and Plate lowers its installed plugin graph into it once.
Creation-time plugins keep inferred installed capabilities; dynamic installs do not pretend to rewrite the static type.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 2026-09-11 lane comparison and the decision page section on extension composition. The files it cites were renamed, so editor-extension.ts, extension-registry.ts and extension-slot.ts are now plugin.ts, plugin-registry.ts and plugin-slot.ts. Rechecked on the live tree the PluginDefinition shape, definePluginSlot, tx.plugins.reconfigure and editor.install staging through stagePluginCandidate, publication rollback in plugin.ts, every definePluginPoint and its consumers, Plate's schema lowering in withPlite.ts, and every production caller of slots, reconfigure, install and defineEditorSchema via git grep.
summary: The job is for plugins to contribute schema, fields, APIs and ordered contributions, and for a host to swap a configurable subtree at runtime with schema, document and APIs publishing together or not at all. The live tree keeps the September design under the plugin rename. definePlugin's definition is flat, with schema as one declaration field. definePluginSlot(key).of(input) names a replaceable subtree, and tx.plugins.reconfigure and editor.install both call stagePluginCandidate inside an active update. Publication rolls back staged activations, fields and APIs on failure. Contribution points have real producers and consumers, namely transferVeto in table, column, details, footnote and upload, DataTransferFormat, and the authored document capability. Plate lowers its plugin graph into one schema foundation plus one application-schema plugin. The strongest cuts are replacing slots with whole-list reconfigure (ProseMirror) or folding install into slots. The first forces a host to rebuild and recompile the whole graph to swap one subtree. The second removes one method but makes every add-after-creation caller predeclare a slot, and the shared staging owner means there is no duplicate authority to remove. Keep the current design.

reconciliation.question: How should typed extensions contribute and reconfigure schema and behavior without duplicate configuration authorities?
reconciliation.reason: Its comparison holds on the renamed plugin owners. Flat descriptors, slots, contribution points and atomic candidate publication still each serve a distinct live consumer, and install and reconfigure share one staging owner.

alternatives: Keeping the current design wins. Each noun serves a live job, with slots for schema swap in the schema-reconfiguration and Yjs examples (taught in editor-api.mdx), contribution points for transfer vetoes and data-transfer formats, and atomic candidate publication for rollback.

Deleting slots and reconfiguring the whole plugin list, as ProseMirror's state.reconfigure does, loses. The host must keep and resubmit the whole graph, which in Plate means the whole lowered plugin set, to swap one subtree. The slot is CodeMirror 6's Compartment, a stable key for one replaceable unit.

Merging editor.install into slots (install as reconfiguring an empty slot) is small and not worth it. Both doors already share stagePluginCandidate, so there is no duplicate authority. Install's only callers are demos and benchmarks that install then uninstall, and CodeMirror 6 likewise keeps appendConfig beside Compartment for add-after-creation.

Deleting contribution points loses. transferVeto (BaseTablePlugin, BaseColumnPlugin, BaseDetailsPlugin, BaseFootnotePlugin, BaseUploadPlugin), DataTransferFormat and the authored document capability would need side registries outside atomic publication.
Restoring a plugin config channel or one overloaded profile factory violates the no-config law and hides distinct schema, resource and replacement laws without removing them.
Moving schema switching into a Plate-only coordinator loses. Raw Plite consumers such as the Yjs schema-upgrade example would rebuild it, and atomic publication is Plite law.

Refusing complete defineEditorSchema plugins in Plate (the hasCompletePluginSchema branch in withPlite.ts) is not needed. No Plate product caller uses one outside withPlite.spec, it is one precedence rule (a complete schema replaces the derived one) rather than two live authorities, and Plate re-exporting the Plite root is distribution's question.
proofLimits: Source read only; schema, contribution and generic inference contracts, browser schema reconfiguration, Yjs transport and compile-cache scale were not run. The decision page and hub still cite the pre-rename extension-* files. plugin.ts carries an uncommitted model-admission hunk (the migrate reader), but it does not bear on this verdict. Dynamic install's product value rests on demos, not a Plate product caller.
